text: , p.1301 Rilmenidine, p.1388 Diuretics Diuretics promote the excretion of water and electrolytes by the kidneys. They are used in the treatment of heart fail- ure or in hepatic, renal, or pulmonary disease when salt and water retention has resulted in oedema or ascites. Diu- retics are also used, either alone, or in association with oth- er drugs, in the treatment of hypertension, although the mechanism for their antihypertensive effect is poorly un- derstood. The principal groups of diuretics are as follows. ◊ Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors such as acetazolamide (p.1875) are weak diuretics and are used mainly to reduce intra-ocular pressure in glaucoma. They are described un- der Miotics, Mydriatics, and Antiglaucoma Drugs, p.1873. ◊ ‘Loop’ or ‘high-ceiling’ diuretics produce an intense, dose-dependent diuresis of relatively short duration. Described in this chapter are Azosemide, p.1222 Furosemide, p.1292 Bumetanide, p.1237 Piretanide, p.1372 Etacrynic Acid, p.1283 Torasemide, p.1415 Etozolin, p.1284 ◊ Osmotic diuretics raise the osmolality of plasma and renal tubular fluid. They are used to reduce or prevent cere- bral oedema, to reduce raised intra-ocular pressure, and in acute renal failure. Described in this chapter are Isosorbide, p.1317 Mannitol, p.1330 ◊ Potassium-sparing diuretics have a relatively weak di- uretic effect and are normally used in conjunction with thi- azide or loop diuretics. Canrenone, eplerenone, potassium canrenoate, and spironolactone are aldosterone antago- nists and are particularly used in conditions where aldos- terone contributes to the pathophysiology. Described in this chapter are Amiloride, p.1209 Spironolactone, p.1400 Canrenone, p.1239 Triamterene, p.1417 Eplerenone, p.1279 Potassium Canrenoate, p.1374 ◊ Thiazides (benzothiadiazines), such as bendroflumethi- azide and hydrochlorothiazide, and certain other com- pounds, such as metolazone, with structural similarities to the thiazides, inhibit sodium and chloride reabsorption in the kidney tubules and produce a corresponding increase in potassium excretion.
